$comment: The core digest task (`double-digest-buffer`) uses the synthetic 512 bp construct
because its three fragments are small enough to check by eye; this file covers
the plasmid-scale path on the real pUC118 fixture, plus the in-silico PCR and
gel tasks that belong to the same bench workflow.

tasks.instruction: I have pUC118.dna in my working directory. Show me the restriction map for EcoRI, HindIII and PvuII on the circular plasmid: where each enzyme cuts, and what fragments each one produces. Then tell me which of the three cuts the plasmid more than once.

I have a 512 bp linear construct in the workspace as a sequence I will paste, but simpler: use the sequence below. Cut it with EcoRI and HindIII together. Do these two enzymes share a reaction buffer, and what fragment sizes should I see on the gel?

{seq:construct}

assertions.note: a shared buffer, so a single-tube digest is fine

THREE fragments, not two: the two site insertions add 6 bp each, so the two sites are 206 bp apart and the digest yields three pieces. This was probed, not reasoned about — the first draft of the fixture documented '200 + 300 bp' and was wrong.
the amplicon's coordinates on the top strand
the tool's verdict word for a single clean product

tasks.instruction: I am running an EcoRI+HindIII double digest of pUC118.dna (full length 3162 bp, in your working directory) on a 1 kb ladder gel. Draw me the expected band pattern, and tell me how many bands I should see and whether the small fragment will be visible.

assertions.note: the gel report names a band count. The value is not pinned: the model chooses how many lanes to draw, and the first version pinned `2 band(s)` from a single-lane draft.
the backbone fragment. Accepted as the exact size or its conventional `~3.1 kb` shorthand: both are correct, and demanding the digits graded how the model chose to round.
the small fragment's exact size — pinned, because it explains the whole answer

assertions.pattern: 1 band|one band|2 band|two band|1 fragment|2 fragment|single .{0,12}band
assertions.note: the band count. The model is EXPECTED to distinguish the two theoretical fragments from the single band a 1 kb-ladder gel actually resolves, so both counts are accepted.

assertions.pattern: not visible|too small|will not|won't|below|faint|run off|dye front|below detection
